enforcementMechanismBuilt.what: scripts/check-ldt-sha-comment-presence.mjs, wired as a new ci.yml job (ldt-sha-comment-presence).
enforcementMechanismBuilt.rule: Fails only when a diff to cloudbuild.publish.yaml changes the _LDT_SHA VALUE without the same diff adding at least one real comment line (a `+` line starting with `#` and carrying content beyond the bare hash). Inert on every other edit to the file -- a different substitution changing, an unrelated comment, pure formatting -- because those never touch the removed/added _LDT_SHA value lines the check looks for.
enforcementMechanismBuilt.whyThisAndNotProse: DEV_PROCESS 0: 'a control that depends on someone remembering is not a control.' The comment convention survived two documented bumps (CTX-PIN, CTX-PIN2) and then silently failed on the next two (#130, #131) the moment nobody was specifically thinking about it -- the exact failure mode the rule describes.
enforcementMechanismBuilt.overBroadnessAvoided: Per the dispatch's explicit constraint, verified with a dedicated fixture ('is not applicable to an edit that never touches the _LDT_SHA value', in test/check-ldt-sha-comment-presence.test.mjs) rather than only asserted in prose.
enforcementMechanismBuilt.wiring: A dedicated job, not added to the existing test job, so it never shares that job's Postgres service or env setup. Runs on pull_request (base.sha vs head) and on push (github.event.before vs head), skipped only on the null-SHA first-push-of-a-branch edge case -- the PR that eventually lands the change still runs the pull_request check in that case.

item2_provenanceRestoredAndEnforcementAn.answerToTheDispatchsQuestion: The mechanism is scripts/check-ldt-sha-comment-presence.mjs, live in ci.yml as of this merge. It is cheap (a single git-diff regex scan, no network, no LDT checkout) and it is now the seventh bump's own admission proof -- PR #137's ldt-sha-comment-presence check-run passed by ADMITTING this lane's own commented bump, which is the first real (non-fixture) positive case it has ever graded. lessons.text: A dispatch's stated baseline for a tracer/instrument can go stale between when it was true and when the dispatch was written, even within the same day, if the tool itself changed underneath it. CTX-B2 fixed the tracer (landed 2026-09-09T23:56) but never touched the file that quotes the tracer's output (cloudbuild.publish.yaml), so every subsequent reader -- including this dispatch -- inherited a number that was correct when written and wrong by the time it was read. Before trusting a dispatch's quoted instrument output, check whether the instrument itself has a more recent close that changed its behavior.

A per-commit staleness-check run (--pin X --main Y for each historical range boundary) gives an AUTHORITATIVE bake-relevance answer for a provenance comment, cheaper and more reliable than inferring reach from git show --stat file lists. Use the real gate script on real range boundaries rather than reasoning about import graphs by hand.

A CLI wrapper that accepts --base/--head but forgets to thread a matching `cwd` through to the git subprocess will silently run against the WRONG repository when cwd differs from the script's own directory -- caught here only because a fixture test using a throwaway repo produced 'Unexpected end of JSON input' (empty stdout from a git command erroring in the wrong directory) rather than a wrong-but-plausible answer. Worth a standing check: any new CLI script that shells out to git needs an explicit, threaded cwd, tested from a directory other than the script's own.

deadEnds.text: Assumed --file cloudbuild.publish.yaml would resolve relative to the script's own repoRoot by default and skipped passing --cwd/cwd explicitly in the first draft of check-ldt-sha-comment-presence.mjs's CLI entrypoint.
